gap: No result ChatGPT got states that CyberPower's own CP1350PFCLCD/CP1500PFCLCD manual (K01-0000162-00) forbids plugging laser printers, paper shredders, copiers, space heaters, vacuums or sump pumps into the battery outlets, says the warranty prohibits using extension cords, outlet strips and surge strips, and names RB1280X2A as the replacement battery where current listings name RB1290X2 for units with serial numbers beginning CXX.
standout_why: I opened CyberPower's CP1500PFCLCDa global page (result 5) and Dell's CP1500PFCLCD listing (result 10). Both already say the unit is Active PFC compatible and name RB1290X2 as the battery, and Dell gives the serial-number condition. Neither page has the manual's list of devices barred from the battery outlets, the warranty ban on extension cords and power strips, or the fact that older units took RB1280X2A. I could not open the cited rival pages for results 1 (cyberpowersystems.com returned HTTP 405), 6 (the Tripp Lite datasheet returned 403) or 15 (eaton.com timed out twice). Result 3, the APC PDF, came back as compressed binary. So I can't say for certain those four pages lack the exclusions. Datasheets and product pages don't usually carry manual warnings, so the finding is probably new, but I haven't proved it.
decides: This confirms the CyberPower CP1500PFCLCD as the budget pick for a PC or AV rack with Active PFC power supplies, and it adds limits the page should state. Plug the conditioner straight into the wall, not into a power strip or surge strip, or you lose warranty cover. Keep laser printers and large motor or heater loads off the five battery outlets and use the five surge-only outlets for them. Before buying a replacement battery, check the serial number: RB1290X2 is for serials starting CXX, and older units list RB1280X2A. The APC SMT1500C keeps its premium place for anyone who wants a network card later: Schneider lists a SmartSlot and graceful shutdown over USB or serial through PowerChute Serial Shutdown. I couldn't open any Eaton or Tripp Lite document, so I have no compatibility facts on the SMART1500LCDT.

findings.label: Active PFC power supply compatibility
findings.value: Supported: "This CyberPower UPS system supports High Efficiency power supplies with Active Power Factor Correction (Active PFC)."
findings.source_title: CyberPower Systems CP1500PFCLCD User Manual (K01-0000162-00), manualsdir mirror
findings.note: Maker's manual, read on a third-party mirror. The CyberPower global CP1500PFCLCDa page also says 'Active PFC Compatibility: Yes'.

findings.label: Devices barred from battery outlets
findings.value: "DO NOT plug a laser printer, paper shredder, copier, space heater, vacuum, sump pump or other large electrical devices into the 'Battery and Surge Protected Outlets'."
findings.source_title: CyberPower Systems CP1500PFCLCD User Manual (K01-0000162-00), manualsdir mirror
findings.note: According to the manual, the unit has 5 battery-plus-surge outlets and 5 surge-only outlets. It also mentions outlets 'Designed for AC Adapters' but doesn't say which group they belong to.

findings.label: Warranty exclusion on daisy-chaining
findings.value: "The warranty prohibits the use of extension cords, outlet strips, and surge strips."
findings.source_title: CyberPower Systems CP1500PFCLCD User Manual (K01-0000162-00), manualsdir mirror

findings.label: Replacement battery, older units (manual K01-0000162-00)
findings.source_title: CyberPower Systems CP1500PFCLCD User Manual (K01-0000162-00), manualsdir mirror
findings.note: The manual lists "CyberPower / RB1280X2A for the CP1500PFCLCD" and RB1270X2A for the CP1350PFCLCD.

findings.label: Replacement battery, current units
findings.value: RB1290X2, quantity 1, for serial numbers beginning with CXX
findings.source_title: CyberPower CP1500PFCLCD PFC Sinewave UPS Systems | Dell USA
findings.note: The serial-number condition comes from Dell's spec table. CyberPower's global CP1500PFCLCDa page also lists RB1290X2 (quantity 1) but gives no serial-number condition. I couldn't open CyberPower's US page (HTTP 405).

findings.label: Remote SNMP/HTTP monitoring
findings.value: "SNMP/HTTP Remote Monitoring: Yes - with optional RMCARD205"
findings.note: This page is for the CP1500PFCLCDa variant. It also lists RMCARD400, RCCARD100, RELAYIO501, RWCCARD100 and RWCCARD101 as optional add-ons. Dell's US listing has the same RMCARD205 line. The page doesn't describe an expansion slot, so I left this out of the pick.

findings.label: Input voltage range before switching to battery
findings.value: 88 to 144 VAC (global CP1500PFCLCDa page); 90 to 140 V (manual K01-0000162-00)
findings.note: The two documents give different figures. The manual says: "If incoming utility voltage drops below 90 volts, or exceeds 140 volts the units automatically switch to battery back-up power."

findings.label: Dell US price
findings.source_title: CyberPower CP1500PFCLCD PFC Sinewave UPS Systems | Dell USA
findings.note: Dell part 8mhpdx. This is a retailer price, not CyberPower's store; ChatGPT showed $239.95 at Newegg.

findings.label: Expansion and shutdown interfaces
findings.value: "SmartConnect Port+SmartSlot"; "Graceful shutdown using serial or USB cables via PowerChute Serial Shutdown"
findings.note: The page says '1440VA/1000W line interactive pure sine wave tower UPS' and 'Replacement battery (1) is available', but the battery model and the list of compatible network cards were in sections that didn't load.

unsourced: APC SMT1500C replacement battery part (RBC7 or APCRBC7): Schneider's page only says 'Replacement battery (1) is available'. The SMT1500C datasheet PDF (result 3) came back as compressed binary that I couldn't read, and only third-party sellers named RBC7.
Which SmartSlot network management cards (for example AP9640 or AP9641) fit the SMT1500C: the communication-options section on se.com didn't load, and no Schneider document I found names them.

Tripp Lite SMART1500LCDT replacement battery (a search snippet said RBC51, two needed), whether it supports a network or SNMP card, and whether its on-battery waveform suits Active PFC supplies: eaton.com timed out three times, and the Mouser datasheet, the S3 datasheet, manualowl and manuals.plus either timed out or returned 403.
Whether the CP1500PFCLCD has an expansion slot that takes RMCARD205: CyberPower's US RMCARD205 page returned HTTP 405, and the Hong Kong page has no compatibility list.
Whether any of the three units works on generator power: neither the CyberPower manual nor the global product page mentions generators.
